articles.title: Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize for her work in international justice
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway (AP) — The South African-born jurist and former U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay, who is currently an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice, won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

articles.title: Man in his 70s critically injured after being struck by vehicle in East York
articles.summary: A man in his 70s suffered critical injuries after being struck by a vehicle on Thursday night.

articles.title: Oshawa mayoral candidates focus on homelessness, downtown concerns at debate
articles.summary: Candidates shared plans to tackle homelessness and revitalize downtown Oshawa during Thursday's debate, hosted by the Greater Oshawa Chamber of Commerce at the Bond St. Event Centre.

articles.title: Mississauga mayoral candidates talk redeveloping Living Arts Centre, platform policy planks
articles.summary: Mississauga mayoral candidates weighed in on the potential Living Arts Centre redevelopment as well as shared various policy ideas and focuses.

articles.title: Woman, 70s, seriously injured in multi-vehicle crash in Etobicoke
articles.summary: A multi-vehicle crash in Etobicoke has sent two people to hospital.

articles.title: ICE officer shoots a man while making an arrest in New York, officials say
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — A federal immigration officer shot a Dominican man in the neck as he drove in a car with a 5-year-old boy Thursday afternoon, officials said. The Department of Homeland Security said it was seeking to arrest the man in a “targeted enforcement operation,” but protesters and local officials decried it as an example of the dangers of the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown.

articles.title: Ontario will officially begin removing Toronto bike lanes on Tuesday
articles.summary: Ontario will begin removing bike lanes from a stretch on Bloor Street W. in Etobicoke on Tuesday, the Ministry of Transportation says.

articles.title: Oshawa museum faces nearly $3K in city fines over homeless encampments on property
articles.summary: A charity that runs a museum in Oshawa has received nearly $3,000 in city fines for allowing "nuisance activity" on its property. It says it needs help, not penalties, to keep the museum safe from vandalism, trespassing and damage.

articles.title: Man dead after industrial accident in Brampton, police say
articles.summary: A man is dead after an industrial accident in Brampton on Wednesday, Peel police say.

articles.title: New documentary about Ridgeway Plaza tackles its negative reputation
articles.summary: 'Meet Me At Ridgeway,' a new film by Mississauga residents, explores the controversial plaza's cultural richness, challenges, opportunities for voter engagement and takeaways for urban planners and the City of Mississauga.
